title: The Vegetarian Curry of Can Tho
segments: Leo arrived at his grandmother's house in the warm Can Tho afternoon. His grandmother, Bà Loan, hugged him tightly. She smiled, "I'm making your favorite chicken curry!" Leo's stomach dropped. "Bà, I have something to tell you... I'm a vegetarian now." Her warm smile slowly faded, and an uncomfortable silence filled the room.

Then, the silence broke. 'But... all I have is the chicken for the curry, and some fish for dinner,' Bà Loan said, her voice soft with concern. She looked around her kitchen at the ingredients she had carefully prepared. 'I don't know how to cook without meat. What will I feed you?'

Because of this, Leo saw the deep worry on his grandmother's face. He didn't want her to be sad. 'Bà,' he said gently, 'what if we go to the market together? We can find some new vegetables and maybe get some inspiration for a vegetarian curry. It could be a new adventure!'

After that, they arrived at the bustling Can Tho market. The air was filled with new smells and sounds. They walked past many stalls, but one vendor with a kind smile caught their eye. She saw their confusion and asked what they were looking for. 'A vegetarian curry?' she said. 'I have the perfect idea!'

Then, following the vendor's advice, they bought sweet potatoes, coconut milk, and fresh lemongrass. Back in Bà Loan's kitchen, the familiar smells of her cooking mixed with the new ingredients. She showed Leo how to chop the vegetables her way, and he showed her a recipe on his phone. They worked together, laughing.

Then, the curry was ready. The whole family gathered around the table. The sweet potatoes and coconut milk smelled wonderful. Everyone took a spoonful, even his uncle who usually only ate meat. He smiled and said it was delicious. Bà Loan looked at Leo, her eyes full of love and pride.
endWrap: You learned that sharing food is about more than just ingredients; it's about sharing love, tradition, and creating new memories together with your family.
